To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the second harmonic light generated by an arbitrary distribution of three-dimensional nonlinear domains can be particularly intense in the forward direction and this effect is due to the scattering of the fundamental light by a single domain.
the optical second harmonic light generated by the weak scattering of light by an arbitrary distribution of nonlinear domains can be particularly intense in the forward direction.

“We show that the weak optical second-harmonic light generated from a non-diffractive random distribution of nonlinear volumes of any shapes can display a particularly strong generation in the forward propagation direction.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the nonlinear optical properties of random media.
the optical properties of a random distribution of three-dimensional nonlinear domains of transparent Sr _{x} Ba _{1-x} Nb _{2} O _{6} crystals.
the study of the nonlinear optical properties of a random distribution of three-dimensional nonlinear domains, which can be of any size and shape.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this phenomenon is a consequence of the scattering of a second harmonic light by a non-diffuse random distribution of nonlinear volumes.
a single nonlinear domain can be considered as an optical scatterer of second harmonic light.
the optical response of a random distribution of non-diffusive nonlinear domains can be described in terms of the response of a single domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a theoretical model able, for the first time, to analyze the optical scattering of light by nonlinear domains of arbitrary shapes and dimensions.

the optical second-harmonic response of a non-diffusing random distribution of nonlinear volumes is a function of the shape, the size, the orientation, the number and the position of the individual nonlinear volumes.

the second harmonic generation from a random distribution can display a particularly strong forward direction, and the scattering of light from a single nonlinear domain can explain the physical origin of the forward enhancement.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the optical response of a single domain can be significantly modified by the presence of the surrounding nonlinear domains, which can result in a significant increase of the second harmonic light generated in the forward direction.
the scattering process is not diffusive.

the optical second-harmonic generation from a random distribution nonlinear domains can be enhanced in the forward direction with respect to the case of a single nonlinear domain, and this effect can be explained in a simple way.
